column15: Independent bottler est. 1948 in Glasgow, family owned, now 3rd generation. Ranges: Remarkable Regional Malts (Big Peat, Timorous Beastie, Scallywag, Rock Island, Epicurean), Old Particular/Provenance/Xtra Old Particular single casks, King of Scots blend, Clan Denny. Bottler peat is unknown by definition; see big-peat row for its heavily peated Islay blended malt. Timorous Beastie (same range) is understood to be a lightly peated Highland blended malt but was not given its own row because the only peat-level source found looked like generic templated retail copy.
Douglas Laing's blended malt of Islay single malts only (Ardbeg, Bowmore, Caol Ila, rare Port Ellen); part of the Remarkable Regional Malts range, heavily peated/smoky.

Added because Douglas Laing bottles Jura single casks. Core production unpeated; limited annual peated runs exist (Superstition, Prophecy) but no such expression is named in this batch's samples, so no rule was added.

Added because Douglas Laing bottles Arran single casks. Core (Lochranza) range unpeated; the "Machrie Moor" line (about 20ppm) is a separate peated expression, produced at sister distillery Lagg since 2019. Owner not independently re-verified this session.
Added because Douglas Laing bottles Ardmore. A rare peated Highland malt; core "Legacy" expression is roughly 80% peated / 20% unpeated malt.
Added because Douglas Laing bottles Bowmore. Traditional floor maltings; peated to roughly 25ppm, between the heavily peated southern-Islay distilleries and lighter styles.
One of the most heavily peated Islay malts, roughly 50-55ppm. Owned by LVMH via The Glenmorangie Company since the 1997 reopening.

Irish whiskey brand (launched 2014) sourcing whiskey mainly from Cooley and finishing/bottling numbered releases. Range mixes unpeated (e.g. Single Pot Still) and heavily peated (No.11 "The Peat Cask" and similar) releases, so house peat is left unknown; see rule for "Peat" pattern.

Taiwan's first single malt distillery (Yuanshan, Yilan). Core range (Classic, Concertmaster, Solist, Podium, etc.) uses unpeated malt imported from Europe. A Peatist Series / Solist Peaty Cask using lightly peated malt also exists, see rules.

Built around Speyside malts, notably Strathisla and Longmorn. Reviews consistently note faint/light peat and smoke rather than a peat-forward profile. Both catalogue brand strings "Chivas" and "Chivas Brothers" are aliased here since nearly all of their sample products are Chivas Regal; Royal Salute (also sometimes filed under "Chivas Brothers") is a separate row relying on its own distinctive in-name alias.
Ultra-premium blended Scotch launched 1953, blended/matured at Strathisla. The standard/Signature range is not peated; a distinct "21 Year Old The Peated Blend" exists, see rule.

Goa, India. Flagship "Brilliance" is unpeated. "Edited" is mildly peated; "Bold" and Select Cask "Peated" use peat carried to Goa from Islay (Bold measured about 25ppm) -- see rules. The "none" here reflects the flagship/default expression, not the whole range.

Blend of malt and corn-heavy grain whisky from a distillery near Mt. Fuji (Fuefuki). Reviews mention "a touch of smoke" but it is unclear whether this is from peated malt or a generic cask/tasting descriptor, so left unknown rather than guessed.
Marriage of Single Pot Still and Single Malt Irish whiskey; explicitly confirmed non-peated.

Melbourne distillery (est. about 2015), matures exclusively in ex-red-wine casks; core range uses unpeated Australian malt. "Peated Finish" is base spirit finished about 18 months in peated Islay casks, see rule -- rated medium rather than heavy since it is a cask finish, not primary peated-malt maturation.

Coastal Highland distillery near Portsoy, just outside Speyside. Core production unpeated. Sibling peated brand "Torfa" (about 20ppm, launched 2014) is a known pair to watch but does not appear among this brand's catalogue samples, so no row/rule was added for it.
Speyside distillery (est. 1895/96), unpeated; most output historically went into blends. Added as the home distillery of The Singleton of Dufftown.
Diageo's Dufftown-sourced Singleton range (introduced 2006, mainly UK/EU market); unpeated, inherits Dufftown's house style.
Central Speyside distillery known for a sulphury/meaty house style from worm-tub condensers (unrelated to peat); one source's own heading calls it "Speyside's Distinctive Unpeated Distillery".

Blanco, Texas whiskey house (own stills plus Kentucky-sourced/blended stock, "Texification" secondary aging); bourbon/rye/blend range so defaultTypeName left empty. Standard corn/rye/malted-barley mash bills; "none" is inferred from American-whiskey convention rather than an explicit statement, hence confidence low.
Orkney distillery founded 1885; malt is "entirely unpeated" per source, matured mainly in ex-bourbon casks.

Owns Glencadam and Tomintoul distilleries and also bottles blends (e.g. "Glen Parker") under its own name; treated as a bottler/owner-company since the catalogue brand spans multiple sub-brands. See glencadam row.
Brechin, Eastern Highlands; opened 1825; unpeated malt.
Heaven Hill's premium bourbon brand (first released 1986); now also includes a Kentucky Straight Rye, so defaultTypeName left empty rather than "bourbon". No peated malt used.
Bardstown/Louisville, Kentucky producer (founded 1935) of bourbon, rye and wheat whiskey; defaultTypeName left empty since the range spans several types. Added as Elijah Craig's parent distillery.
Nara-prefecture blend combining Japanese whisky with malts sourced from around the world (Kamiki Shuzo / Helios Distiller); no information found on whether peated malt is used.

Created by Eamonn Jones and Gerald Erdrich; consistently marketed/reviewed as an intensely, heavily peated Islay-style whisky. Source distillery is not disclosed (one source notes peat is also used outside Islay), so no parentSlug is set even though retail listings brand it "Islay"; defaultTypeName left empty since sourcing/type description is inconsistent (single malt vs multi-distillery).

Kurayoshi Distillery, Tottori (Matsui Shuzo, founded 1910, distilling its own whisky since 2017). Core Sakura Cask / Mizunara Cask NAS releases are unpeated; "The Peated" is a separate expression, see rule. Covers both catalogue brand strings "The Matsui" and "Matsui".

Scotland's oldest independent bottler, founded 1895 in Elgin; catalogue brand string is spelled "Gordonmacphail" (no spaces/ampersand). Also owns Benromach (reopened 1998) and built Cairn Distillery (2022).

Added because Gordon & MacPhail bottles Tormore single casks. Built 1958-60, the first new Speyside distillery of the 20th century; unpeated, historically mostly used in blends. Acquired by Elixir Distillers in 2022.
Added because Gordon & MacPhail bottles Glenlivet ("Smith's Glenlivet") single casks. Founded 1824; classic light, unpeated Speyside style; process water filters through peat-free granite.

Sleat peninsula, Isle of Skye; first distilled 2017. House style described as "elegantly rugged peat"; the Legacy Series' Allt Gleann is cited at roughly 77ppm malt phenol. Both this batch's samples ("Torabhaig The Legacy", "Torabhaig Allt Gleann") are from the peated Legacy Series; the catalogue brand string for this row is actually "The Legacy Series", aliased here.
Roughly 150-year-old recipe recreated in 2012 by A.D. Rattray: 40% Speyside/Highland malt with 60% Lowland grain. The base blend is unpeated; a separate "Peated Reserve" exists, see rule.

Indian whisky blend of grain spirit and imported Scotch malt (launched 1995; Pernod Ricard's top-selling brand by volume since 2001). One source's tasting note mentions "a touch of smoke" but this is not confirmed to be peat-derived, so left unknown.

Houston, Texas (founded 2010, Houston's first legal whiskey distillery). Portfolio spans Outlaw Bourbon, Harris County high-rye Bourbon, Premium American and Straight Rye, so defaultTypeName left empty. Standard American mash bills, no peated malt.

Coastal Eastern Highlands distillery (founded 1962) where the Deveron River meets the North Sea. Malt used for blending spirit is fully unpeated; malt used for the distillery's own single malt ("The Deveron") is lightly peated. The owner never bottles under the name "Macduff" itself, only as "The Deveron"/"Glen Deveron"; "Macduff" as a bottling name is used only by independent bottlers.

Owner's own-bottled name for Macduff distillery's single malt. Sold as "Glen Deveron" historically (notably for the Italian market under Martini Rossi) and as "The Deveron" since October 2015; lightly peated. Catalogue sample "Glen Deveron" is the older name for this same brand.

Produced by Niche Drinks in Derry (first Irish whiskey bottled there in over 100 years) for Luxco, a US company now owned by MGP Ingredients. Range spans a blend and an 8-year-old single malt, so defaultTypeName left empty. Derry is technically in Northern Ireland (UK) but the product is marketed under the "Irish whiskey" geographic category, so countryCode is set to IE consistent with that convention. No source found confirming peat status, left unknown rather than assumed. Catalogue brand string for this row is "Luxco".

Very little web presence found beyond an EU retailer (WineStyle) listing "Sour Mash", "Black Label" and "White Label" variants, suggesting an American-style whiskey, but no distillery, owner or country could be confirmed.
No web presence found; catalogue gives only "Conciere" with no further detail. Treated as a generic own-label; peat left unknown rather than assumed "none" since no citation could be opened.
Not researched (budget prioritised to larger brands). "Single Barrel" / "20 Barrels Selection Batch 1" naming suggests an American-style small-batch whiskey but origin is unconfirmed.
Not researched (budget); single-product own label with no distinguishing sample information.
Not researched (budget). "Gwalarn" is a Breton word (northwest wind); countryCode inferred from the name only, not verified.

Not researched (budget). Sample "Johnny Hepp Alsacien" names Alsace explicitly; countryCode inferred from the name only. A real Alsatian spirits house named Hepp exists but this was not confirmed this session.
Not researched (budget); no distinguishing information in the catalogue sample.
Not researched (budget); "Moulin" is ambiguous (French for "mill"; also a place name in Highland Scotland), so countryCode left empty rather than guessed.
Not researched (budget); generic "Old ___'s" own-label naming, origin unconfirmed.

Not researched (budget). "Ragtime" + "Rye" is a strongly American-coded name; countryCode/defaultTypeName inferred from the name only. Peat left unknown per no-citation policy (American rye is conventionally unpeated but this was not verified for this specific brand).
Not researched (budget). "Shefford" is a town in Bedfordshire, England; countryCode inferred from the name only.
Not researched (budget). Sample "Turning Point Rye" -- defaultTypeName inferred from the name; countryCode left empty since rye whiskey naming is used both in the US and Canada.
Not researched (budget). "Crater Lake" is a well-known Oregon, US landmark; countryCode/defaultTypeName inferred from the name, peat left unknown per no-citation policy.

Blackpool, England distillery (est. 2019, Halewood-backed). Produces both peated and unpeated English malt spirit (EM/PEM/PBM plus corn/rye/wheated mashes); flagship "Distiller's Cut" is the bourbon-inspired, non-"Peated"-labelled single malt. See rule for explicitly "Peated"-labelled releases.
